nameplate.purpose: The masthead title (the front page's h1); 40px at 900px and below, 38px compact on library and issue pages, 22px in the footer.

display.purpose: The lead issue's title on the front page, balanced wrap. One per page.

headline.purpose: Section heads such as "Earlier issues"; 28px at 720px and below.

title.purpose: Issue titles in the archive list; 21px on phones.

deck.purpose: Newsreader italic cover line under the lead title, Soft Ink, max 30ch.

body.purpose: Reading paragraphs, Soft Ink, max 65ch. Short interface text uses the page default of 18px at 1.4.

dateline.purpose: Issue number, date and page count with tabular lining figures, joined by Pencil Grey middle dots.

link.purpose: Standalone links such as "Read online" and "Contents", underlined in Stone Line.

button.purpose: Uppercase button labels; a file size inside the button drops to 500 weight, 0.04em, tabular, 75% opacity.

label.purpose: Uppercase navigation (13px in the masthead) and form legends and field labels (11px). Never a kicker above a heading.

data.purpose: Literal machine strings only: PDF file names, @handles, SHA or build hashes.

shadows.name: lead-cover-lift
shadows.purpose: Under the front page's lead cover; the only lift on the front page.

shadows.name: lead-cover-lift-hover
shadows.purpose: Lead cover on hover, with a 6px rise over 0.35s.

shadows.name: issue-hero-cover
shadows.purpose: The cover on the issue page.

shadows.name: page-thumbnail
shadows.purpose: Page thumbnails in the issue page's page grid.

shadows.name: reader-page
shadows.purpose: Pages on the reader's stage (light mode).

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Colour, border and underline-colour transitions on links, buttons, chips and nav.

motion.name: ease-paper
motion.purpose: Default easing for cover and thumbnail rises, section fades and progress bars.

motion.name: ease-lift
motion.purpose: The front page's lead cover rise (350ms).

motion.name: section-fade
motion.value: 550ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), opacity 0 to 1 with a 10px rise, fill-mode backwards
motion.purpose: Section entrance on library and issue pages; the front page lead has no entrance.

narrative.overview:
The site is the printed magazine's own register: a front page where the newest issue leads, a library that lists the rest, and a reader that turns the pages. It is set like a publication, not assembled like an app. Book paper ground, one ink, one red. Structure comes from ruled lines of graded weight and from one strict two-column grid, never from boxes, tints or shadows. The covers are the only pictures and the only objects that lift off the page.

Two typefaces do the talking. Newsreader carries the nameplate, every title, the italic cover lines and the reading text. IBM Plex Sans Condensed runs the machinery: navigation, buttons, datelines, links and every fact in a row, always with tabular figures. IBM Plex Mono is held back for literal machine strings such as file names and @handles. Density is calm: large type, generous section gaps, short lists, nothing competing with the cover.

The front page (redesigned October 2026) is the system's newest and cleanest expression: the lead on the two-column register grid, one dateline band, square ink buttons that carry their file sizes, underlined text links, and a ruled list of earlier issues opened by the page's single heavy rule. The library, issue and reader pages share the tokens and components but still carry older devices (label kickers above headings, a red tab section marker, monospace metadata) that this document does not adopt. New surfaces follow the front page.
keyCharacteristics: Book paper ground, press ink, and one red that marks state and place.
Rules of graded weight do the work that boxes and cards do elsewhere.
One two-column grid holds the lead and every list row, so titles align down the page.
Newsreader speaks; Plex Sans Condensed operates, with tabular lining figures for every fact.
Square corners everywhere; a soft paper lift only under covers and page images.
Self-hosted faces only; nothing loads from a third-party host.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red means "here" or "now": current location, hover, focus, selection, progress. Headings, rules and body text never take it at rest, and it fills an area only as a button's hover state.

rules.name: The Paper Ground Rule
rules.body: Pages sit on Book Paper with no section tints or banded backgrounds. Proof Sheet is the only raised paper, and only for the download box and source cards.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Newsreader speaks (nameplate, titles, decks, reading); Plex Sans Condensed operates (nav, buttons, datelines, links, meta). A third voice appears only as data.

rules.name: The Tabular Facts Rule
rules.body: Every number that sits in a row or a button (issue numbers, dates, page counts, file sizes, issue totals) is Plex Sans Condensed with tabular lining figures, so columns of facts line up.

rules.name: The Real Data Mono Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is legitimate only for literal machine strings: a file name, an @handle, a SHA or build hash. Dates, counts, page numbers, breadcrumbs, captions, status strips and labels are never monospace; the front page uses none.

rules.name: The One Grid Rule
rules.body: The lead and every list row share the same two columns, so cover, metadata and titles align down the whole page. A new section joins that grid rather than inventing its own.

rules.name: The Rule Weights Rule
rules.body: Rules carry structure, graded by weight: a Hairline Grey 1px between rows, 1px ink to open a section or top a dateline band, 2px ink under the masthead (followed by a 3px gap and a 1px ink line, a double rule) and over the footer, and one 3px ink rule per page to open the archive list.

rules.name: The Paper Lift Rule
rules.body: Only printed objects and floating cards cast a shadow, always soft and offset downward. A shadow never stands in for a border, a section or a button state.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: No radius anywhere (0px). Softness comes from the paper, not the corners.

dos: Do set every page on Book Paper (#F7F4EC) in Press Ink (#1A1A1A), and let Cover Red (#C1121F) mark only state and place: hover, focus, the current nav item, selection.
Do separate with rules by weight: a Hairline Grey 1px between rows, 1px ink to open a section, 2px ink under the masthead and over the footer, and one 3px ink rule per page for the archive list.
Do put the lead and every list row on the one two-column grid (min(24rem, 38%) and 1fr, gutter clamp(40px, 5vw, 72px)), collapsing to one column at 720px.
Do set every row fact (issue number, date, page count, file size) in Plex Sans Condensed with tabular lining figures, joined by a Pencil Grey middle dot.
Do carry a file's size inside the button that downloads it, in a right-aligned slot reserved at 4.6em.
Do keep every target at least 44px (50px for the lead's PDF buttons) and keep the 2px red focus outline at a 3px offset.
Do use IBM Plex Mono only for literal machine strings: a PDF file name, an @handle, a SHA or build hash.
Do draw icons as inline SVG line icons on a 24px grid, stroked in currentColor at 1.6–1.7, with no fill.
donts: Don't put a small uppercase label above a heading. The older pages' red "LIBRARY", "ISSUE NO. 2 · COVER STORY" and "THIS WEEK" labels, and the blue section labels above contents headlines, are defects; the heading carries itself.
Don't mark sections with the red 32×8px tab on a red hairline; open a section with a 1px ink rule.
Don't set dates, counts, page numbers, breadcrumbs, captions or status strips in monospace to look technical.
Don't round anything: buttons, chips, fields, boxes and covers are square (0px).
Don't put a shadow on buttons, rules, text or boxes; the soft paper lift belongs to covers, page images and floating cards.
Don't use Index Blue (#2F5D8A) as a second accent for links, buttons or headings; it is annotation only.
Don't use Unicode arrows or other glyphs as icons, as the library's "Read →" and the issue page's monospace ←/→ still do.
Don't add colour literals outside the ten tokens for text or rules, as the older print box (#2B2B2B) and reader placeholder (#8a867d) still do.
